items.stem: What was President Kennedy's "New Frontier" program?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál fue el programa de "Nueva Frontera" del Presidente Kennedy?

choices.text: Domestic agenda to improve education, end discrimination, and reach the moon
choices.textEs: Agenda doméstica para mejorar educación, acabar discriminación y llegar a la luna

choices.text: A domestic agenda to improve education, end discrimination, and advance science
choices.textEs: Un plan para expandir territorio estadounidense adquiriendo nuevas tierras en el Pacífico

choices.text: Landing on the moon would demonstrate American technological superiority
choices.textEs: Una estrategia militar enfocada en construir armas nucleares para defensa

choices.text: Send American volunteers to developing nations to provide assistance
choices.textEs: Un programa económico que eliminó todo gasto federal en programas sociales

items.explanation: Kennedy's New Frontier was a domestic reform agenda that called for better education, civil rights progress, aid for the elderly, and major scientific goals such as reaching the moon. C is wrong because it describes only the moon goal, and D is wrong because it describes the Peace Corps rather than the whole program. The New Frontier linked Cold War competition with domestic reform at home.
items.explanationEs: La Nueva Frontera de Kennedy propuso mejorar la educación, proporcionar atención médica para los ancianos, terminar la discriminación racial y poner un hombre en la luna. También creó el Cuerpo de Paz para enviar voluntarios estadounidenses a naciones en desarrollo.

B is tempting because the moon goal was part of Kennedy's program, but the New Frontier was bigger than the space race alone, and C is wrong because it describes the effect of his assassination. Many New Frontier ideas later influenced legislation passed under Lyndon Johnson.

choices.text: The complete absence of any emergency preparation in New Orleans
choices.textEs: The complete absence of any emergency preparation in New Orleans

choices.text: A deliberate government decision to flood certain neighborhoods to protect others
choices.textEs: A deliberate government decision to flood certain neighborhoods to protect others

The disaster showed how infrastructure failure can turn a storm into a far larger human catastrophe.

items.explanation: Kennedy created the Peace Corps in 1961 to send American volunteers to developing nations to help with education, health, and agriculture. The program used service and goodwill as tools in the Cold War struggle for influence.

items.stem: How did President Kennedy's space program goal reflect Cold War competition?

choices.text: Domestic agenda to improve education, end discrimination, and reach the moon
choices.textEs: Kennedy propuso una misión conjunta con la Unión Soviética para explorar el espacio

choices.text: Send American volunteers to developing nations to provide assistance

C is wrong because it states the goal but not its broader meaning, and B is wrong because the Peace Corps addressed a different part of the Cold War. The space race turned science into a contest for global prestige.
items.explanationEs: Después de que los soviéticos lanzaran el Sputnik (1957) y pusieran al primer hombre en el espacio (1961), Kennedy se comprometió a aterrizar un hombre en la luna antes del fin de la década. Este objetivo trataba de probar la superioridad tecnológica y científica estadounidense sobre la Unión Soviética en la Guerra Fría.

items.explanationEs: El asesinato de Kennedy el 22 de noviembre de 1963 impactó y traumatizó a la nación. El Presidente Johnson usó el duelo nacional para impulsar la agenda legislativa de Kennedy.

choices.textEs: Tennessee's cities grew primarily through industrial development while national trends favored service economies

choices.text: Tennessee's urban-rural divide mirrors national patterns where large cities grow while rural areas face economic decline
choices.textEs: Tennessee's urban-rural divide mirrors national patterns where large cities grow while rural areas face economic decline

items.explanation: Tennessee reflects a national pattern in which major cities grow and diversify while many rural areas struggle economically and politically. A is wrong because Tennessee is not unique in facing urban-rural tension. The state's geography helps explain why its politics can look different in cities than in the countryside.

choices.textEs: Nashville and Memphis were historically exempt from Tennessee's conservative political tradition

A is wrong because race matters but does not fully explain the difference by itself. Their politics reflect a wider urban-rural divide seen across the United States.

items.stem: Kennedy's establishment of the Peace Corps in 1961 reflected which Cold War strategy?
items.stemEs: Kennedy's establishment of the Peace Corps in 1961 reflected which Guerra Fría strategy?

choices.text: Military deterrence through the deployment of American troops in developing nations
choices.textEs: Military deterrence through the deployment of American troops in developing nations

choices.text: Winning hearts and minds in developing countries through volunteerism and development assistance to counter Soviet influence
choices.textEs: Winning hearts and minds in developing countries through volunteerism and development assistance to counter Soviet influence

choices.text: Economic competition with the Soviet Union through trade agreements with newly independent African and Asian nations
choices.textEs: Economic competition with the Soviet Union through comercio agreements with newly independent African and Asian nations

choices.text: Intelligence gathering in foreign countries through the presence of civilian volunteers
choices.textEs: Intelligence gathering in foreign countries through the presence of civilian volunteers

items.explanation: The Peace Corps reflected a Cold War 'hearts and minds' strategy by sending volunteers to help developing countries and build goodwill toward the United States. D is wrong because it was not mainly an intelligence operation. Kennedy used volunteer service as a peaceful way to compete with Soviet influence.
items.explanationEs: The Peace Corps reflected a Guerra Fría 'hearts and minds' strategy by sending volunteers to help developing countries and build goodwill toward the United States. D is wrong because it was not mainly an intelligence operation. Kennedy used volunteer service as a peaceful way to compete with Soviet influence.

items.stem: Johnson's announcement in March 1968 that he would **NOT** seek reelection reflected which political reality?
items.stemEs: Johnson's announcement in March 1968 that he would NOT seek reelection reflected which political reality?

choices.text: Johnson was in poor health and his doctors advised against the physical demands of campaigning
choices.textEs: Johnson was in poor health and his doctors advised against the physical demands of campaigning

choices.text: Growing opposition to the Vietnam War had severely damaged his popularity and he faced a serious primary challenge
choices.textEs: Growing opposition to the Guerra de Vietnam had severely damaged his popularity and he faced a serious challenge within his own party

choices.text: The Republican Party had already selected a stronger candidate whom Johnson could not defeat
choices.textEs: The repúblicaan Party had already selected a stronger candidate whom Johnson could not defeat

choices.text: The Constitution's 22nd Amendment prevented him from serving another term
choices.textEs: The Constitución's 22nd enmienda prevented him from serving another term

items.explanation: Johnson's 1968 decision not to run again reflected how deeply the Vietnam War had damaged his popularity and split his own party. D is wrong because the Constitution still allowed him to seek another full term. Vietnam weakened support for the same president who had passed the Great Society.
items.explanationEs: Johnson's 1968 decision not to run again reflected how deeply the Guerra de Vietnam had damaged his popularity and split his own party. D is wrong because the Constitución still allowed him to seek another full term. Vietnam weakened support for the same president who had passed the Gran Sociedad.

items.stem: How did New Frontier proposals influence later domestic policy even when not fully enacted under Kennedy?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo New Frontier proposals influence later política interna even when not fully enacted under Kennedy?

choices.text: Sending American volunteers abroad to support education, health, and development projects
choices.textEs: Sending American volunteers abroad to support education, health, and development projects

choices.text: They provided legislative foundations that Johnson advanced through Great Society programs
choices.textEs: They provided legislative foundations that Johnson advanced through Gran Sociedad programs

choices.text: It traumatized the nation and created sympathy that helped pass his legislative agenda
choices.textEs: It traumatized the nation and created sympathy that helped pass his legislative agenda

choices.text: A domestic agenda to improve education, end discrimination, and advance science
choices.textEs: A domestic agenda to improve education, end discriminación, and advance science

items.explanation: Even when Kennedy did not get all of his proposals passed, the New Frontier shaped later laws by giving Johnson ideas and political groundwork to build on. B is wrong because the Peace Corps was only one program, not the broader legacy. This continuity shows how presidential agendas can matter even beyond one administration.
items.explanationEs: Even when Kennedy did not get all of his proposals passed, the New Frontier shaped later laws by giving Johnson ideas and political groundwork to build on. B is wrong because the Peace Corps was only one program, not the broader legacy. This continuity shows how presidential agendas can matter even beyond one administration.

items.stem: The 1965 Immigration Act represented a major change from previous U.S. immigration policy by —

choices.text: Banning all immigration from Asia and Latin America
Requiring all immigrants to come from Northern and Western Europe
Eliminating all numerical limits on immigration
Replacing national-origin quotas with a system based on family ties and skills

items.explanation: The Hart-Celler Act, enacted as Public Law 89-236 on October 3, 1965 (79 Stat. 911), fundamentally restructured U.S. immigration by replacing the national-origin quota system established by the Immigration Act of 1924 with a preference system based on family reunification and occupational skills. Choice A is wrong because the Hart-Celler Act did not ban immigration from Asia or Latin America; it actually opened pathways for immigrants from those regions previously excluded by national-origin caps. Choice B is wrong because the prior quotas, not the 1965 law, heavily favored Northern and Western Europeans; the new law ended that preference. Choice C is wrong because the law maintained numerical limits on overall immigration while changing the selection criteria. The demographic transformation that followed significantly altered the ethnic composition of the United States.
items.explanationEs: La Ley Hart-Celler, promulgada como Ley Pública 89-236 el 3 de octubre de 1965 (79 Stat. 911), reestructuró fundamentalmente la inmigración en EE. UU. al reemplazar el sistema de cuotas por origen nacional establecido por la Ley de Inmigración de 1924 con un sistema de preferencias basado en la reunificación familiar y las habilidades laborales. La opción A es incorrecta porque la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad de 1965 no prohibió la inmigración de Asia o América Latina; en realidad abrió caminos para inmigrantes de esas regiones que anteriormente habían sido excluidos por los límites de cuotas nacionales. La opción B es incorrecta porque las cuotas previas por origen nacional, no la ley de 1965, favorecían ampliamente a los europeos del norte y del oeste; la nueva ley eliminó esa preferencia. La opción C es incorrecta porque la ley mantuvo límites numéricos a la inmigración total mientras cambiaba los criterios de selección. La transformación demográfica que siguió alteró significativamente la composición étnica de los Estados Unidos.

items.stem: How did Kennedy's New Frontier agenda reflect a departure from Eisenhower's domestic priorities?

choices.text: The New Frontier called for increased federal investment in education, space exploration, foreign aid through the Peace Corps, and civil rights — a more activist approach than Eisenhower's
The New Frontier reduced federal spending dramatically to balance the budget, reversing Eisenhower's expansion of programs like the Interstate Highway System
Kennedy's New Frontier focused exclusively on military preparedness and eliminated all social welfare programs from the federal budget
The New Frontier represented a return to isolationism by ending foreign aid and withdrawing from international organizations

items.explanation: Kennedy's New Frontier was an activist domestic and foreign agenda: it proposed federal aid to education, created the Peace Corps (1961), pledged to land a man on the moon, and challenged the complacency of the Eisenhower era with calls for national sacrifice and service.

items.stem: How did the Peace Corps, established by Kennedy in 1961, reflect the goals of the New Frontier?

choices.text: The Peace Corps was a military organization designed to train soldiers for counterinsurgency operations in developing nations
The Peace Corps embodied the New Frontier's call to service, sending volunteers to developing nations to advance economic development and goodwill as peaceful Cold War competition
The Peace Corps was established to provide employment for American workers during a recession rather than to assist foreign countries
The Peace Corps focused exclusively on rebuilding European nations still recovering from the devastation of World War II

items.explanation: Kennedy's Peace Corps sent American volunteers — educators, engineers, health workers — to developing nations, combining genuine humanitarian goals with strategic Cold War aims: demonstrating that democracy could improve lives more effectively than communism.

items.stem: Why did Kennedy commit the United States to landing a man on the Moon by the end of the 1960s?

choices.text: Kennedy was primarily motivated by scientific curiosity and had no strategic or political reasons for the moon commitment
Kennedy committed to the moon program because NASA scientists had already completed all preparatory work and needed only funding to launch the mission
Following Soviet achievements like Sputnik and Gagarin's orbit, Kennedy used the moon goal to reassert American technological prestige and demonstrate democratic capitalism's vitality
Kennedy announced the moon commitment as part of a treaty with the Soviet Union to cooperate on space exploration

items.explanation: After Gagarin's 1961 orbit humiliated the U.S., Kennedy chose the moon as a goal the Soviets had not yet achieved, framing Apollo as a demonstration that democratic free enterprise could outperform Soviet central planning in a visible, dramatic competition.

items.stem: How did Kennedy's approach to racial discrimination differ from that of the Eisenhower administration?

choices.text: Kennedy was more reluctant than Eisenhower to use federal power to address racial discrimination and avoided civil rights entirely
Kennedy opposed civil rights legislation and relied on the states to address racial inequality without federal intervention
Kennedy and Eisenhower had identical approaches to civil rights; both aggressively enforced desegregation throughout their presidencies
Kennedy issued executive orders addressing discrimination in federal housing and employment and proposed comprehensive civil rights legislation — more proactive than Eisenhower's

items.explanation: Kennedy signed Executive Order 10925 (1961) banning discrimination by federal contractors, federalized the National Guard during the Ole Miss crisis (1962), and proposed comprehensive civil rights legislation in June 1963 — a notably more interventionist stance than Eisenhower's reluctant enforcement.

items.stem: How did Kennedy's New Frontier reflect a generational shift in American political leadership?

choices.text: Kennedy's emphasis on youth, vigor, and sacrifice — embodied in his 'ask not' inaugural — signaled a shift from Eisenhower's cautious leadership to a younger, idealistic vision
Kennedy's policies were indistinguishable from those of older leaders and represented no meaningful generational change
Kennedy's New Frontier explicitly rejected the accomplishments of the New Deal and sought to dismantle all programs created by FDR
Kennedy won the presidency primarily based on his military record, with no connection to generational or cultural appeal

items.explanation: Kennedy, at 43 the youngest elected president, deliberately projected youth and vigor as symbols of national renewal; his inaugural address's call to service resonated with baby boomers and represented a self-conscious generational changing of the guard.

items.stem: How did Kennedy's federal education initiatives reflect New Frontier priorities?

choices.text: Kennedy eliminated all federal involvement in education, arguing it should be handled entirely by states and local communities
Kennedy's education initiatives focused exclusively on creating new private religious schools as alternatives to public education
Kennedy sought to increase federal aid to public schools to improve educational quality and address Cold War concerns about American competitiveness
Kennedy's education proposals were unanimously approved by Congress with no opposition and implemented immediately

items.explanation: Kennedy proposed federal aid to elementary and secondary education as a Cold War competitiveness measure and equity investment, but the bills stalled in Congress due to battles over aid to parochial schools and segregated Southern districts — issues LBJ would resolve with the 1965 Elementary and Secondary Education Act.

items.stem: The political transformation of Tennessee from a competitive state (represented by Al Gore) to a reliably Republican one reflects —
items.stemEs: The political transformation of Tennessee from a competitive state (represented by Al Gore) to a reliably repúblicaan one reflects:

choices.text: Economic changes that made Tennessee more prosperous, and research shows prosperous states lean Republican
choices.textEs: Economic changes that made Tennessee more prosperous, and research shows prosperous states lean repúblicaan

choices.text: The realignment of white Southern voters from the Democratic Party that accelerated after the 1960s and completed in the 1990s-2000s
choices.textEs: The realignment of white Southern voters from the democrático Party that accelerated after the 1960s and completed in the 1990s-2000s

choices.text: The success of Tennessee Republicans in disenfranchising Democratic-leaning voter groups
choices.textEs: The success of Tennessee repúblicaans in disenfranchising democrático-leaning voter groups

choices.text: In-migration of Republican voters from Northern states who shifted Tennessee's political balance
choices.textEs: In-migration of repúblicaan voters from Northern states who shifted Tennessee's political balance

items.explanation: Tennessee's shift from competitive to reliably Republican reflects the long realignment of white Southern voters away from the Democratic Party after the 1960s. D is wrong because migration from the North was not the main reason. By the 1990s and 2000s, this regional realignment was largely complete.
items.explanationEs: Tennessee's shift from competitive to reliably repúblicaan reflects the long realignment of white Southern voters away from the democrático Party after the 1960s. D is wrong because migration from the North was not the main reason. By the 1990s and 2000s, this regional realignment was largely complete.

items.stem: Kennedy's New Frontier programs faced significant opposition in Congress despite Democratic majorities. Which of the following best explains why congressional opposition limited Kennedy's domestic agenda?
items.stemEs: Los programas de la Nueva Frontera de Kennedy enfrentaron una oposición significativa en el Congreso a pesar de las mayorías demócratas. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor por qué la oposición del Congreso limitó la agenda interna de Kennedy?

choices.text: Republicans controlled both the House and Senate throughout Kennedy's presidency, blocking any Democratic legislation from reaching the floor for a vote
choices.textEs: Los republicanos controlaban tanto la Cámara como el Senado durante toda la presidencia de Kennedy, lo que hacía imposible aprobar cualquier legislación demócrata.

choices.text: Conservative Southern Democrats with key committee chairs joined Republicans to block the civil rights measures and federal program expansions at the heart of Kennedy's agenda
choices.textEs: Los demócratas sureños conservadores, que controlaban las presidencias de los comités clave y se oponían a los derechos civiles y a la expansión de los programas federales, formaron una coalición de bloqueo con los republicanos que impidió que gran parte de la agenda de la Nueva Frontera se aprobara.

choices.text: Kennedy refused to introduce any civil rights legislation, which alienated liberal Democrats who then voted against all of his other programs in retaliation.
choices.textEs: Kennedy se negó a presentar cualquier legislación de derechos civiles, lo que alienó a los demócratas liberales que luego votaron en contra de todos sus otros programas en represalia.

choices.text: The Democratic Party had collapsed as a political force by 1961, leaving Kennedy unable to count on any congressional allies for his domestic agenda.
choices.textEs: El Partido Demócrata se había derrumbado como fuerza política para 1961, dejando a Kennedy incapaz de contar con aliados del Congreso para su agenda interna.

items.explanation: The Democratic Party of the early 1960s was internally divided between Northern liberals (who supported New Frontier expansion) and conservative Southern Democrats who controlled key committee chairmanships and opposed civil rights legislation, federal aid to education, and healthcare programs. This 'conservative coalition' of Southern Democrats and Republicans could block most liberal legislation regardless of formal Democratic majorities. Kennedy's narrow 1960 victory also left him without a strong electoral mandate. Option A is factually incorrect — Democrats had majorities. Option C misidentifies Kennedy's stance; he did support civil rights legislation, though cautiously. Option D describes a later dynamic (post-1965).
items.explanationEs: El Partido Demócrata de principios de los años 60 estaba internamente dividido entre liberales del Norte y demócratas sureños conservadores que controlaban presidencias clave de comités y se oponían a la legislación de derechos civiles, la ayuda federal a la educación y los programas de atención médica. Esta 'coalición conservadora' podía bloquear la mayoría de la legislación liberal independientemente de las mayorías demócratas formales. La opción A es factualmente incorrecta. La opción C identifica mal la postura de Kennedy. La opción D describe una dinámica posterior.

items.stem: The Peace Corps, established by Kennedy in 1961, represented a new approach to American foreign policy. Which of the following best explains how it differed from prior instruments of U.S. foreign policy during the Cold War?
items.stemEs: El Cuerpo de Paz, establecido por Kennedy en 1961, representó un nuevo enfoque de la política exterior estadounidense. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor cómo difería de los instrumentos anteriores de la política exterior de Estados Unidos durante la Guerra Fría?

choices.text: The Peace Corps deployed soft power through people-to-people assistance, contrasting with Cold War instruments that relied on military aid, covert operations, and government-to-government ties
choices.textEs: El Cuerpo de Paz desplegó poder blando a través de asistencia directa de desarrollo de persona a persona a nivel de base, contrastando con los instrumentos anteriores de la Guerra Fría que dependían de ayuda militar, operaciones encubiertas y relaciones gobierno a gobierno.

choices.text: The Peace Corps focused exclusively on wealthy European nations, aiming to prevent them from aligning with the Soviet Union through economic development assistance.
choices.textEs: El Cuerpo de Paz se centró exclusivamente en las naciones europeas ricas, con el objetivo de evitar que se alinearan con la Unión Soviética a través de la asistencia para el desarrollo económico.

choices.text: The Peace Corps was a military training program that prepared volunteers to serve as guerrilla fighters in nations threatened by communist insurgencies.
choices.textEs: El Cuerpo de Paz era un programa de entrenamiento militar que preparaba a los voluntarios para servir como guerrilleros en naciones amenazadas por insurgencias comunistas.

choices.text: The Peace Corps was primarily an intelligence-gathering operation that used development workers as cover for CIA agents collecting information on communist movements.
choices.textEs: El Cuerpo de Paz era principalmente una operación de recopilación de inteligencia que utilizaba a los trabajadores del desarrollo como cobertura para agentes de la CIA que recopilaban información sobre los movimientos comunistas.

items.explanation: Prior Cold War instruments (military aid, CIA covert operations, arms sales) relied on hard power — supporting friendly governments militarily regardless of their democratic legitimacy. The Peace Corps represented a 'soft power' approach: rather than supporting governments, it deployed ordinary Americans into communities to provide direct grassroots development assistance, building goodwill at the people-to-people level rather than the government-to-government level. This was a genuine departure from covert operations and military aid as primary foreign policy tools. Option B is incorrect — the Peace Corps specifically targeted developing nations. Option C is factually inaccurate. Option D misidentifies the innovation — the Peace Corps was not primarily an intelligence program.
items.explanationEs: Los instrumentos anteriores de la Guerra Fría (ayuda militar, operaciones encubiertas de la CIA, ventas de armas) dependían del poder duro. El Cuerpo de Paz representó un enfoque de 'poder blando': en lugar de apoyar gobiernos, desplegó a estadounidenses comunes en comunidades para proporcionar asistencia directa de desarrollo de base, construyendo buena voluntad a nivel pueblo a pueblo. La opción B es incorrecta. La opción C es factualmente inexacta. La opción D identifica mal la innovación.

items.stem: Kennedy's 1961 moon mission commitment — 'We choose to go to the moon in this decade' — was made at a moment when the United States was behind the Soviet Union in the space race. Which of the following best explains the strategic reasoning behind this specific, ambitious timeline?
items.stemEs: El compromiso de Kennedy en 1961 con la misión lunar —'Elegimos ir a la luna en esta década'— se hizo en un momento en que Estados Unidos estaba detrás de la Unión Soviética en la carrera espacial. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor el razonamiento estratégico detrás de este cronograma específico y ambicioso?

choices.text: Kennedy chose the moon mission because the United States already had overwhelming superiority in space technology and the mission was a low-risk way to demonstrate established American leadership.
choices.textEs: Kennedy eligió la misión lunar porque Estados Unidos ya tenía una abrumadora superioridad en tecnología espacial y la misión era una forma de bajo riesgo de demostrar el liderazgo estadounidense establecido.

choices.text: Kennedy's primary motivation was economic — the moon mission would stimulate the American economy through defense contracts, with the Cold War competition being a secondary justification.
choices.textEs: La motivación principal de Kennedy era económica: la misión lunar estimularía la economía estadounidense a través de contratos de defensa, siendo la competencia de la Guerra Fría una justificación secundaria.

choices.text: By choosing a destination where neither nation had yet achieved any milestone, Kennedy reset the competition to a level playing field while committing a specific deadline that would sustain public funding and national focus across administrations.
choices.textEs: Al elegir un destino donde ninguna nación había logrado ningún hito todavía, Kennedy reinició la competencia en un campo de juego nivelado mientras comprometía un plazo específico que sostendría la financiación pública y el enfoque nacional a través de las administraciones.

choices.text: Kennedy publicly proposed that the United States and Soviet Union collaborate on the moon mission, reasoning that joint achievement would be more impressive than competitive victory.
choices.textEs: Kennedy propuso públicamente que Estados Unidos y la Unión Soviética colaboraran en la misión lunar, razonando que el logro conjunto sería más impresionante que la victoria competitiva.

items.explanation: By committing to a destination (the moon) where neither superpower had yet achieved any milestone, Kennedy essentially reset the competition to a level playing field. The Soviets led in near-Earth orbital achievements; the moon mission was a new race where both sides were starting from scratch. The ten-year deadline also created public accountability that sustained funding across administrations. Option A reverses the logic — Kennedy chose the moon precisely because the U.S. was behind in existing competitions. Option B misidentifies the motivation; economic development was secondary. Option D is factually incorrect — Kennedy did not propose abandoning competition.
items.explanationEs: Al comprometerse con un destino (la luna) donde ninguna superpotencia había logrado ningún hito todavía, Kennedy esencialmente reinició la competencia en un campo de juego nivelado. Los soviéticos lideraban en logros orbitales cercanos a la Tierra; la misión lunar era una nueva carrera donde ambos lados partían desde cero. La opción A invierte la lógica. La opción B identifica mal la motivación. La opción D es factualmente incorrecta.

items.stem: Kennedy's approach to civil rights has been described by historians as 'cautious' and even 'reluctant' in his first two years. Which of the following best explains why a president who opposed racial discrimination moved slowly on civil rights legislation?
items.stemEs: El enfoque de Kennedy hacia los derechos civiles ha sido descrito por los historiadores como 'cauteloso' e incluso 'reticente' en sus primeros dos años. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor por qué un presidente que se oponía a la discriminación racial avanzó lentamente en la legislación de derechos civiles?

choices.text: Kennedy took no action on civil rights whatsoever during his presidency, waiting entirely for Congress to initiate any legislative or executive steps.
choices.textEs: Kennedy dependía de los votos del Congreso demócrata sureño para su agenda legislativa más amplia y temía que la legislación agresiva de derechos civiles destruyera la coalición que necesitaba para los programas de educación, económicos y espaciales.

choices.text: Kennedy privately supported racial segregation and only appeared to support civil rights for political purposes during election campaigns.
choices.textEs: Kennedy apoyaba privadamente la segregación racial y solo aparentaba apoyar los derechos civiles con fines políticos durante las campañas electorales.

choices.text: Kennedy believed civil rights were exclusively a state matter and that the federal government had no constitutional authority to address racial discrimination.
choices.textEs: Kennedy creía que los derechos civiles eran exclusivamente un asunto estatal y que el gobierno federal no tenía autoridad constitucional para abordar la discriminación racial.

choices.text: Kennedy relied on Southern Democratic votes and feared civil rights legislation would destroy the congressional coalition he needed for education, economic, and space programs
choices.textEs: Kennedy no tomó ninguna acción sobre los derechos civiles durante su presidencia, esperando completamente que el Congreso iniciara cualquier paso legislativo o ejecutivo.

items.explanation: Kennedy depended on Southern Democratic votes for his entire legislative agenda — aid to education, economic programs, the space program. Pushing civil rights legislation hard in 1961–62 risked destroying the Southern Democratic coalition that Kennedy needed for everything else. He used executive action (executive orders on federal employment discrimination, federal contracts) rather than legislation to make incremental progress while preserving congressional relationships. Only after Birmingham (spring 1963) did he commit to major civil rights legislation. Option B is historically inaccurate — Kennedy did support civil rights. Option C misidentifies the mechanism. Option D is factually wrong — he did act through executive orders.
items.explanationEs: Kennedy dependía de los votos demócratas sureños para toda su agenda legislativa. Presionar fuertemente por la legislación de derechos civiles en 1961–62 arriesgaba destruir la coalición demócrata sureña que Kennedy necesitaba para todo lo demás. Utilizó la acción ejecutiva en lugar de la legislación para hacer avances incrementales. Solo después de Birmingham (primavera de 1963) se comprometió con la legislación principal de derechos civiles. La opción B es históricamente inexacta. La opción C identifica mal el mecanismo. La opción D es factualmente incorrecta.

items.stem: Kennedy's proposal for federal aid to education was blocked in Congress partly due to the issue of aid to religious (Catholic) schools. Which of the following best explains the constitutional dimension of this controversy?
items.stemEs: La propuesta de Kennedy de ayuda federal a la educación fue bloqueada en el Congreso en parte debido al tema de la ayuda a las escuelas religiosas (católicas). ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor la dimensión constitucional de esta controversia?

choices.text: The controversy arose because Congress believed public schools were adequately funded and that federal aid would only improve Catholic schools at the expense of public education
choices.textEs: La controversia surgió porque el Congreso creía que las escuelas públicas ya estaban adecuadamente financiadas y que la ayuda federal solo mejoraría las escuelas católicas a expensas del público.

choices.text: The Tenth Amendment reserved education entirely to state governments, making any federal education funding unconstitutional regardless of which schools received it
choices.textEs: La Décima Enmienda reservaba la educación completamente a los gobiernos estatales, haciendo que cualquier financiación federal de la educación fuera inconstitucional independientemente de qué escuelas la recibieran.

choices.text: Kennedy personally opposed federal funding for education, believing schools should be supported entirely through local taxation and private contributions
choices.textEs: Kennedy se opuso a cualquier ayuda a las escuelas públicas porque creía que la educación debería financiarse enteramente de forma privada a través de matrículas.

choices.text: Including religious schools risked violating the First Amendment, while excluding them alienated Catholic voters — a dilemma Kennedy could not resolve without losing key political allies
choices.textEs: Incluir a las escuelas religiosas en la ayuda federal corría el riesgo de violar la Cláusula de Establecimiento de la Primera Enmienda, mientras que excluirlas alienaba a los electores católicos, creando un dilema constitucional y político que Kennedy no podía resolver sin perder aliados liberales o votantes católicos.

items.explanation: The Establishment Clause of the First Amendment prohibits government from establishing or favoring religion. Kennedy — himself Catholic — was in an awkward position: if federal education aid included religious schools, it might violate the Establishment Clause; if it excluded them, Catholic leaders (a core Democratic constituency) would oppose the bill. This constitutional tension was compounded by the political dynamics of Kennedy being the first Catholic president and needing to appear neutral on church-state issues. Option A is incorrect — the controversy was specifically constitutional and political, not purely about school quality. Option B misidentifies the constitutional issue. Option C is incorrect — Kennedy supported aid to public schools.
items.explanationEs: La Cláusula de Establecimiento de la Primera Enmienda prohíbe al gobierno establecer o favorecer la religión. Kennedy —él mismo católico— estaba en una posición incómoda: si la ayuda federal a la educación incluía escuelas religiosas, podría violar la Cláusula de Establecimiento; si las excluía, los líderes católicos se opondrían al proyecto de ley. La opción A es incorrecta. La opción B identifica mal el problema constitucional. La opción C es incorrecta.

items.stem: Kennedy's New Frontier rhetoric promised bold action, but his actual legislative achievements by 1963 were limited. Which of the following best explains the gap between the New Frontier's aspirations and its legislative record?
items.stemEs: La retórica de la Nueva Frontera de Kennedy prometía una acción audaz, pero sus logros legislativos reales para 1963 eran limitados. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor la brecha entre las aspiraciones de la Nueva Frontera y su historial legislativo?

choices.text: Kennedy deliberately chose not to pursue any domestic legislation, believing that executive action alone was sufficient to transform American society.
choices.textEs: Kennedy optó deliberadamente por no buscar ninguna legislación interna, creyendo que la acción ejecutiva sola era suficiente para transformar la sociedad estadounidense.

choices.text: Kennedy focused exclusively on foreign policy and never sent domestic legislative proposals to Congress during his presidency.
choices.textEs: Kennedy se centró exclusivamente en la política exterior y nunca envió propuestas legislativas internas al Congreso durante su presidencia.

choices.text: Structural constraints — including a slim electoral mandate, the conservative coalition blocking progressive legislation
choices.textEs: Las restricciones estructurales —incluyendo un mandato electoral estrecho, la coalición conservadora bloqueando la legislación progresista y las demandas de política exterior de la Guerra Fría consumiendo capital político— impidieron que la mayoría de las propuestas de la Nueva Frontera se aprobaran a pesar de las genuinas aspiraciones de Kennedy.

choices.text: Kennedy's New Frontier proposals failed because he was personally opposed to federal spending and refused to fund the programs he publicly endorsed.
choices.textEs: Las propuestas de la Nueva Frontera de Kennedy fracasaron porque él personalmente se oponía al gasto federal y se negó a financiar los programas que públicamente respaldaba.

items.explanation: The gap between rhetoric and results reflects structural constraints: Kennedy's slim 1960 electoral margin gave him little political capital; the conservative coalition of Southern Democrats and Republicans controlled key committee chairs and could block most progressive legislation; and Kennedy chose to pursue Cold War foreign policy priorities (space, Berlin, Cuba) that consumed his political energy and public capital. His strongest domestic achievements came through executive action, not legislation. Option A is too strong — some legislation did pass. Option B is incorrect — Kennedy did seek congressional action. Option D misidentifies the primary obstacles; fiscal conservatism was one factor but not the dominant one.
items.explanationEs: La brecha entre la retórica y los resultados refleja restricciones estructurales: el estrecho margen electoral de Kennedy en 1960 le dio poco capital político; la coalición conservadora controlaba las presidencias clave de los comités; y Kennedy eligió priorizar la política exterior de la Guerra Fría. Sus logros domésticos más sólidos vinieron a través de la acción ejecutiva, no de la legislación. La opción A es demasiado fuerte. La opción B es incorrecta. La opción D identifica mal los obstáculos principales.

items.stem: Kennedy's executive order establishing the President's Committee on Equal Employment Opportunity (1961) addressed racial discrimination in federal employment. Which of the following best explains why Kennedy chose executive action rather than legislation for this initiative?
items.stemEs: La orden ejecutiva de Kennedy que estableció el Comité del Presidente sobre Igualdad de Oportunidades de Empleo (1961) abordó la discriminación racial en el empleo federal. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor por qué Kennedy eligió la acción ejecutiva en lugar de la legislación para esta iniciativa?

choices.text: Kennedy used executive orders because they required a two-thirds congressional majority — a higher bar than simple legislation — demonstrating stronger commitment.
choices.textEs: Kennedy usó órdenes ejecutivas porque requerían una mayoría de dos tercios del Congreso —un estándar más alto que la legislación simple— demostrando un mayor compromiso.

choices.text: Executive action allowed Kennedy to advance civil rights within executive authority without the congressional coalition backlash that legislation would have triggered, protecting political capital
choices.textEs: La acción ejecutiva permitió a Kennedy avanzar en los derechos civiles dentro de la clara autoridad del poder ejecutivo sin desencadenar la reacción de la coalición del Congreso que habría provocado la legislación de derechos civiles, preservando el capital político para otras prioridades.

choices.text: The Constitution explicitly prohibited Congress from passing civil rights legislation, leaving executive orders as the only available tool for addressing discrimination.
choices.textEs: La Constitución prohibía explícitamente al Congreso aprobar legislación de derechos civiles, dejando las órdenes ejecutivas como la única herramienta disponible para abordar la discriminación.

choices.text: Executive orders applied automatically to all levels of government and all private employers, making them more comprehensive than any legislation could have been.
choices.textEs: Las órdenes ejecutivas se aplicaban automáticamente a todos los niveles de gobierno y a todos los empleadores privados, haciéndolas más completas de lo que podría haber sido cualquier legislación.

items.explanation: Executive orders allow the president to act within the executive branch without congressional approval. By targeting federal employment specifically, Kennedy could advance civil rights incrementally in an area where presidential authority was clear, without triggering the Southern Democrat coalition backlash that civil rights legislation would provoke. This approach produced real change in a limited sphere while preserving legislative coalitions for other priorities. Option A is factually incorrect — executive orders do not require congressional approval. Option C is correct but incomplete — the broader reason was congressional obstruction, not just the Constitution. Option D misrepresents the nature of executive orders.
items.explanationEs: Las órdenes ejecutivas permiten al presidente actuar dentro del poder ejecutivo sin aprobación del Congreso. Al apuntar específicamente al empleo federal, Kennedy podía avanzar en los derechos civiles de manera incremental en un área donde la autoridad presidencial era clara, sin desencadenar la reacción de la coalición demócrata sureña que provocaría la legislación de derechos civiles. La opción A es factualmente incorrecta. La opción C es correcta pero incompleta. La opción D representa incorrectamente la naturaleza de las órdenes ejecutivas.

items.stem: Historians debate whether Kennedy's New Frontier programs represented a genuine philosophical break from Eisenhower's 'dynamic conservatism' or merely a rhetorical difference with similar underlying policies. Which of the following evidence best supports the argument for continuity rather than change?
items.stemEs: Los historiadores debaten si los programas de la Nueva Frontera de Kennedy representaron una ruptura filosófica genuina del 'conservadurismo dinámico' de Eisenhower o meramente una diferencia retórica con políticas subyacentes similares. ¿Cuál de las siguientes evidencias respalda mejor el argumento de continuidad en lugar de cambio?

choices.text: Both maintained large defense budgets, accepted the New Deal, and pursued anti-communist containment — suggesting their differences were more rhetorical and stylistic than substantively directional
choices.textEs: Tanto Kennedy como Eisenhower mantuvieron grandes presupuestos de defensa, aceptaron el marco del New Deal sin una expansión dramática y persiguieron la contención anticomunista, lo que sugiere que sus políticas reales diferían más en retórica y estilo que en dirección fundamental.

choices.text: Kennedy dramatically increased the federal budget, created new cabinet agencies, and fundamentally restructured the federal government's relationship with state and local governments
choices.textEs: Kennedy aumentó dramáticamente el presupuesto federal, creó docenas de nuevas agencias a nivel de gabinete y reestructuró fundamentalmente la relación entre el gobierno federal y los estados.

choices.text: Kennedy aggressively pursued civil rights legislation in his first year, passing major bills that Eisenhower had refused to support throughout his two terms
choices.textEs: Kennedy avanzó agresivamente en la legislación de derechos civiles en su primer año, aprobando proyectos de ley importantes que Eisenhower se había negado a apoyar.

choices.text: Kennedy explicitly rejected the Eisenhower defense budget, cutting military spending in half and redirecting funds entirely to domestic social programs
choices.textEs: Kennedy rechazó explícitamente el presupuesto de defensa de Eisenhower, reduciendo el gasto militar a la mitad y redirigiendo los fondos enteramente a programas sociales internos.

items.explanation: Both Kennedy and Eisenhower maintained large defense budgets, accepted the basic New Deal welfare state framework without dramatically expanding it, used Keynesian demand management, and were deeply committed to anti-communist containment in foreign policy. Kennedy's actual legislative achievements in domestic policy were modest — his tax cut proposal was supply-side in nature, and he did not pass major new social programs. The contrast was more in rhetoric, style, and youth than in fundamental policy direction. Option B actually supports the change argument. Option C supports the change argument regarding civil rights. Option D would support difference — Kennedy's rhetorical vision was distinctly more expansionist.
items.explanationEs: Tanto Kennedy como Eisenhower mantuvieron grandes presupuestos de defensa, aceptaron el marco básico del Estado de bienestar del New Deal sin expandirlo dramáticamente, y estuvieron profundamente comprometidos con la contención anticomunista. Los logros legislativos reales de Kennedy en política doméstica fueron modestos. La opción B en realidad respalda el argumento del cambio. La opción C respalda el argumento del cambio sobre los derechos civiles. La opción D respaldaría la diferencia.

items.stem: Kennedy's assassination in November 1963 led directly to the passage of major legislation in 1964 and 1965 that Kennedy had proposed but could not pass. Which of the following best explains the mechanism by which his death changed the political landscape?
items.stemEs: El asesinato de Kennedy en noviembre de 1963 llevó directamente a la aprobación de la legislación principal en 1964 y 1965 que Kennedy había propuesto pero no podía aprobar. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor el mecanismo por el cual su muerte cambió el panorama político?

choices.text: Kennedy's death caused his congressional opponents to change their policy beliefs, resulting in formerly conservative politicians voting for liberal legislation out of genuine conviction.
choices.textEs: La muerte de Kennedy hizo que sus opositores en el Congreso cambiaran sus creencias políticas, resultando en que políticos anteriormente conservadores votaran por legislación liberal por convicción genuina.

choices.text: Public grief over Kennedy's death shifted American public opinion so dramatically that Congress had no choice but to pass all of his proposals to avoid electoral defeat.
choices.textEs: El duelo público por la muerte de Kennedy cambió la opinión pública estadounidense tan dramáticamente que el Congreso no tuvo más remedio que aprobar todas sus propuestas para evitar la derrota electoral.

choices.text: Kennedy's assassination triggered special elections that replaced conservative Democratic senators with liberal ones, giving Lyndon Johnson the votes he needed for new legislation.
choices.textEs: El asesinato de Kennedy desencadenó elecciones especiales que reemplazaron a senadores demócratas conservadores con liberales, dándole a Lyndon Johnson los votos que necesitaba para nueva legislación.

choices.text: Johnson invoked Kennedy's legacy to frame resistance to civil rights and anti-poverty legislation as dishonoring a fallen president, overcoming the Southern Democrats who had blocked Kennedy's agenda
choices.textEs: Lyndon Johnson invocó hábilmente el legado mártir de Kennedy para enmarcar la oposición a la legislación de derechos civiles y anti-pobreza como una falta de respeto a un presidente caído, superando la misma coalición demócrata sureña que había bloqueado los proyectos de ley de Kennedy combinando culpa, duelo y su propio dominio de las relaciones del Congreso.

items.explanation: Kennedy's assassination created a political environment in which opposing his legislative agenda could be framed as disrespecting his martyred memory. Lyndon Johnson — a master congressional strategist with deep Southern Democratic ties — skillfully invoked Kennedy's legacy to overcome the very Southern Democratic opposition that had blocked Kennedy's bills. Johnson used guilt, grief, and his own congressional relationships to pass the Civil Rights Act (1964), the Economic Opportunity Act (1964), and eventually the Voting Rights Act (1965). Option A is factually incorrect — opposition politicians did not suddenly agree. Option B overstates the role of public opinion shifts alone. Option C incorrectly identifies the mechanism — the congressional composition changed little immediately.
items.explanationEs: El asesinato de Kennedy creó un entorno político en el que oponerse a su agenda legislativa podía enmarcarse como falta de respeto a su memoria de mártir. Lyndon Johnson —un maestro estratega del Congreso con profundos lazos demócratas sureños— invocó hábilmente el legado de Kennedy para superar la propia oposición demócrata sureña que había bloqueado los proyectos de ley de Kennedy. La opción A es factualmente incorrecta. La opción B sobreestima el papel de los cambios en la opinión pública solos. La opción C identifica incorrectamente el mecanismo.
